unit_audit.exact_source_text_lf:
\GAGASubsection{3. Analytic sheaves}{gaga:no:3}

The definition of analytic sheaves given in \GAGACite{2}, Expos\'e XV extends immediately to an analytic space $\mathrm{X}$: an analytic sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ is simply a sheaf of modules over the sheaf of rings $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{X}}$, in other words, a sheaf of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{X}}$-modules (cf. \GAGACite{18}, no.~6).

Let $\mathrm{Y}$ be a closed analytic subset of $\mathrm{X}$. For every $x\in\mathrm{X}$, let $\mathcal{J}_x(\mathrm{Y})$ be the set of $f\in\mathcal{H}_{x,\,\mathrm{X}}$ whose restriction to $\mathrm{Y}$ vanishes in a neighbourhood of $x$. The $\mathcal{J}_x(\mathrm{Y})$ form a sheaf of ideals $\mathcal{J}(\mathrm{Y})$ of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{X}}$; hence $\mathcal{J}(\mathrm{Y})$ is an analytic sheaf. The quotient sheaf $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{X}}/\mathcal{J}(\mathrm{Y})$ vanishes outside $\mathrm{Y}$, and its restriction to $\mathrm{Y}$ is precisely $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{Y}}$ by the definition of the induced structure. We may therefore identify it with $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{Y}}$; cf. \GAGACite{18}, no.~5.

\GAGATarget{gaga:prop:1}\textsc{Proposition 1}. --- a) \emph{The sheaf $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{X}}$ is a coherent sheaf of rings} (\GAGACite{18}, no.~15).

b) \emph{If $\mathrm{Y}$ is a closed analytic subspace of $\mathrm{X}$, then $\mathcal{J}(\mathrm{Y})$ is a coherent analytic sheaf (that is, a coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{X}}$-modules in the sense of \GAGACite{18}, no.~12).}

When $\mathrm{X}$ is an open subset of $\mathbf{C}^n$, these results are due to K. \textsc{Oka} and H. \textsc{Cartan}; cf. \GAGACite{1}, Theorems~1 and~2, and \GAGACite{2}, Expos\'es XV--XVI. The general case reduces immediately to this one. Since the question is local, we may suppose that $\mathrm{X}$ is a closed analytic subset of an open set $\mathrm{U}\subset\mathbf{C}^n$. Then $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{X}}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{U}}/\mathcal{J}(\mathrm{X})$, and, by what precedes, $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{U}}$ is a coherent sheaf of rings and $\mathcal{J}(\mathrm{X})$ is a coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{U}}$. It follows that $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{X}}$ is coherent; cf. \GAGACite{18}, no.~16. Assertion b) is proved in the same way.

Other examples of coherent analytic sheaves are the sheaves of germs of sections of fibre spaces with vector-space fibre (cf. \GAGAInternalRef{gaga:no:20}{no.~20}) and the sheaves of germs of automorphic functions (\GAGACite{3}, Expos\'e XX).

unit_audit.exact_role: States coherence of the analytic structure sheaf and coherence of every closed analytic subspace's vanishing ideal, with a local reduction to Oka-Cartan on open subsets of complex affine space.

Identifies local rings as reduced Noetherian quotients of convergent power-series rings, states germ reconstruction, characterizes simple points by regularity, and relates analytic components and dimension to minimal primes and Krull dimension.

gaga:def:1.ambient_data: A set X with a topology and a subsheaf H_X of the sheaf C(X) of germs of complex-valued functions.
gaga:def:1.axiom_H_I: X admits an open cover by pieces isomorphic, with induced topology and sheaf, to analytic subsets of complex affine spaces carrying the no. 1 topology and sheaf.
gaga:def:1.axiom_H_II: The topology of X is Hausdorff.
gaga:def:1.consequence: Because H_X is a subsheaf of a function sheaf, its stalks have no nonzero nilpotents. The definition must not be silently modernized to nonreduced analytic spaces.

gaga:prop:1.part_a: The analytic structure sheaf H_X is a coherent sheaf of rings; in current Stacks language H_X is coherent as an H_X-module.
gaga:prop:1.part_b: For every closed analytic subspace Y of X, its vanishing ideal J(Y) is a coherent H_X-module.
gaga:prop:1.local_reduction: Locally write X as a closed analytic subset of an open Omega in C^n and Y as a closed analytic subset with ideals I_X subset I_Y. Oka-Cartan gives coherence of O_Omega, I_X, and I_Y; coherent quotients and change of rings give coherence of O_X=O_Omega/I_X and J_Y=I_Y/I_X.

missing_analytic_foundations.statement: Local zero-set definition, induced holomorphic-function sheaf, holomorphic maps, charts, induced analytic subspaces, and products for reduced Serre analytic spaces.
On an open subset of C^n, O and vanishing ideals of closed analytic subsets are coherent.
The convergent power-series ring C{z_1,...,z_n} is Noetherian.
Local homomorphisms between analytic local C-algebras arise contravariantly from holomorphic germ maps; local-algebra isomorphisms recover analytic germs.
A reduced analytic germ is smooth/simple of dimension n exactly when its local analytic ring is regular of dimension n.
Radical ideals/minimal primes of a local analytic algebra correspond to analytic subgerms/irreducible components.
An irreducible analytic local algebra of analytic dimension r is finite over C{z_1,...,z_r}, yielding equality with Krull dimension.
